items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: I went with Earl Hines right after that.

ctx.x: When did -- you were in Tommy Miles' Band in what year?

It must have been '31, '32 -- '31, '30 because I went with Earl Hines right after that. Jimmy Mundy was the first guy to go with Earl Hines. But I'll tell you how this kind of came about. We used to play a battle of music all the time with a band from Baltimore, and this band was called the Ambassadors.

Now, in this band there was a trumpet player, high note trumpet player. He was very flashy, and his name was Stevenson. But he went with Lunceford later on. items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] How much did you get paid in Earl Hine's band? [INTERVIEWEE] Oh, nothing hardly. Let me see. In the early '30's, I think I made about $44.00 a week.

ctx.x: It was real encouragement, you know, for you to do things. And that's why they tried to get me with Cab's band back there then, but I wouldn't go, you know. I told them I wouldn't go. I said if I got with your band, you think I'd get those kind of solos to play. And Cab said, yeah, that makes sense. You'd make money but you wouldn't be -- I didn't need money then. I was foot loose and free, you know, so I didn't need no lot of money and I just enjoyed playing. I really almost didn't go with Lunceford from Earl…
How much did you get paid in Earl Hine's band?

Oh, nothing hardly. Let me see. In the early '30's, I think I made about $44.00 a week. And the most we got in there was I think -- when we worked in the Grand Terrace was about $68.00 a week. That's the most we ever got and we worked from 10 to 4. And we played three long shows a night, about hour and a half shows. And was all music and was all bang, bang, you know.
